title: The Foundations of Cost-Sensitive Learning
venue: Proceedings of the Seventeenth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-01)
conclusions: Formalizes when a two-class cost matrix is 'reasonable' (c10>c00, c01>c11) and shows the optimal decision rule is a threshold p* on P(j=1|x) derived from the cost matrix (Eq. 2).

Proves Theorem 1/Theorem 2: how to rebalance the proportion of negative vs. positive training examples so that a standard (non-cost-sensitive) learner's default 0.5 threshold implements a target cost-based threshold p*, without changing within-class example distributions.

Argues empirically/theoretically that rebalancing training data has little effect on classifiers produced by standard Bayesian and decision-tree learners (base-rate changes mostly shift only the estimated class prior).
Shows the impurity criterion used for decision-tree splitting (e.g. 2*sqrt(p(1-p))) is invariant to changes in class base rates (Theorem 3), so rebalancing does not help tree growing either.
Recommends instead: learn a probability estimator on the data as given, then apply the cost-based threshold (Eq. 1/2) directly at decision time, adjusting/calibrating probability estimates if needed.

The whole analysis is per-example expected-cost minimization via a fixed decision threshold; it contains no notion of a global/set-level count or quota on how many test examples may receive a given label.
our_use: main.tex line ~209, in the 'Cost-sensitive and imbalanced training' paragraph: '...Reweighting or reshaping the loss changes which examples are emphasized: cost-sensitive thresholds \citep{elkan2001foundations}, focal loss \citep{lin2017focal}, ... None of it guarantees the prediction count; the realized number of constrained-class predictions remains a free outcome.' The paper is cited (via \citep, parenthetical, appropriate) purely as the canonical reference for per-example cost-sensitive decision thresholds, one item in a list of loss-reshaping/threshold techniques that (correctly) do not provide any count guarantee.
